doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

title: Music at funerals and the Gretna and Algiers parks
summary: Laine describes march music after the burial, the Lee Benevolent and Owls clubs, and regular park and racetrack jobs across the river.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Oh no. Rough. Anything go long. Anything. Anything. Ragtime, anything. Long coming back.
The last barrel march we would play is when they put the body in the tomb. Or in the hole. Yeah. See. Then...
This is 20 years ago, this picture.

Then the minister or priest or whatever... He had that taken. He's held a ceremony over his body. They mean a Christian. Right after that we'd march all out, we'd walk out, not march, walk out to the gate of the cemetery and the organizations would form up right there. Then we'd start from there. See. We'd start right from there coming on back to the hall.
And the organization marched back with you then? Oh yes.
Bring the organization right back to the hall. Yeah. Oh yeah.

What organizations you said, the Crockett Fire Company and what other organizations did you charge for? Who else did you play for? The Davy Crockett and then who else? Who else had the funerals? Lee Benevolent.
Lee Benevolent. They were a very large organization. Was that on this side of the river or over there? No, over in Gretna. Over there. Over in Gretna, yeah. L-E-E.

Yes. I played the funerals over there. And I used to play also, there was a club over there, a very good club but it wasn't very strong, the Owls, they called themselves the Owls. They were out on the river bank. They had their clubhouse out on the river bank. They'd parties, funerals and the balls and all like that. I'd play for that, see? See? Then I played the Suburban Racetrack. That was my main spot, the Suburban Racetrack. Where was that? Over in McDonneville.

McDonneville, yeah. And Cramer's lot was in Algiers. They had them going, see? Yeah. And the Crescent Park was up in Gretna. See? Yeah. Well, I'd have bands put in there every Sunday or Saturday night in them three parks, regular. Regular. Races and all that sort of stuff at the Suburban Park I played. Oh yeah. Yeah.
